title: Position & equity realisation
description: Five questions on EQR and OOP strategy.

questions.prompt: Approximately what range does solver work assign to EQR for an in-position player?
questions.explanation: IP players realise ~105–120% of their raw equity. OOP players realise ~80–95%. The ~10–25% gap is the structural value of position.

questions.prompt: A hand with 35% raw equity IP often outperforms the same hand with 35% raw equity OOP because of equity realisation.
questions.explanation: EQR IP > 100% turns 35% raw equity into ~40% effective; EQR OOP < 100% turns it into ~30%. That gap flips many borderline decisions.

questions.prompt: Which strategic adjustments should an OOP player make? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Check more often, especially on dynamic textures.
Use smaller sizings to keep the pot manageable.
Use the check-raise as a primary aggression vehicle.
C-bet at the same frequency as IP because the math is identical.
Float wider on the flop to build big pots.

questions.explanation: OOP should check more, size smaller, and rely on check-raises. C-bet frequency drops OOP because there's no information advantage; floating wider OOP is a leak.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a reason IP players realise more equity than OOP players?

choices.text: IP players see villain's action before deciding.
IP players can take free cards by checking back.
IP players are dealt stronger starting hands.
OOP players must commit chips before knowing villain's plan.

questions.explanation: Cards are random — position doesn't change starting-hand strength. The information advantage and the option to check back are the real mechanisms.

questions.prompt: You hold JTs in the SB facing a BTN open. The chart says JTs is a 3-bet rather than a flat-call. The most likely reason is:

choices.text: JTs is too strong for a flat-call OOP.
Flatting OOP would force you to realise reduced EQR; 3-betting takes initiative and often wins preflop.
JTs blocks AKo, AQo, and KQs strongly.
Flat-calling is forbidden from the SB.

questions.explanation: OOP cold-calls take a heavy EQR penalty. A 3-bet bypasses postflop play more often (preflop fold equity) and builds a low-SPR pot when called. JTs's modest blocker effect is a side benefit, not the main reason.
